title: An Em groove with space in it
aim: Play a two-bar Em groove where the rests and the muted note matter as much as the pitches.
meta: Leith Bass Space · Four-string bass in standard tuning

blocks.text: This line sits on the root of Em and climbs to the fifth, B. The eighth rest in bar 1 and the muted note in bar 2 give it its shape: without them, it becomes a scale.

blocks.title: Figure 1. Em groove
blocks.caption: Orange numbers under the staff are fretting-hand fingers. The x is a muted note: rest your fretting fingers on the A string without pressing, then pluck.

items: Play bar 1 alone with a metronome at a slow tempo. Stop the open E cleanly for the rest.
Add bar 2 and let the dotted quarter E ring for its full length before the muted note.
Loop both bars. When it feels steady, try it with a drum loop.

rows: The silence after the two E notes, then the quick lift up to B.
A short, percussive muted note that sounds like part of the drums.
